extraction.notes: Whole staff working document read (pages 1-33). Text-file page numbers are the printed page numbers plus two. All passages on the digital transformation part of the Reform Agenda (sections 1.1.1, 1.1.5, 1.2) were extracted; elsewhere only passages meeting the materiality test, with doubtful cases flagged theme_doubtful. No Chapter 2 material: the document has no passage on the rights of EU or foreign workers, social security coordination or EURES; the wage guarantee for workers in bankrupt companies and the labour market skills mismatch are outside the run record's Chapter 2 boundary. Left out as not material under rules 0.4: the automated court case management system (pages 13 and 24, back-office); the Organised Crime and Corruption Track Record platform and the e-platform for organised crime data (pages 14-15, enforcement data platforms); the asset management case software (page 15); digital forensic analysts (pages 14 and 24); the state aid management information system (page 19); the integrated financial management information system and IT capacity for public finance (pages 29 and 31, back-office); Intelligent Transport Systems and e-freight (pages 11, 22 and 27); digital skills, curricula and teacher training (pages 18, 21 and 26, not linked to an in-scope recommendation); general references to investing in a digital future and the twin transition (pages 12 and 16); the ICT priority area of the smart specialisation strategy (page 18). Item -0005 repeats the Early Warning System step also extracted from Annex I (MKD-EU-2024-007-0022). Period covered not given; left empty. Second-pass check done (G3 condition 2), see review/RUN-2026-01/second_pass/.

items.stated_text: The Reform Agenda identifies challenges such as low productivity growth, characterised by the prevalence of low added value branches throughout its economy, a complex legal and regulatory environment hindering the ease of doing business, limited access to finance for SMEs, slow innovation and technology adoption, gaps in digitalisation affecting both business operations and the public sector structural problems of the labour market, such as the skills mismatch between labour market requirements and educational qualifications.
items.summary: The Reform Agenda identifies challenges including slow technology adoption and gaps in digitalisation affecting businesses and the public sector.

location.section: Part 1 > 1.1 Assessment of the relevance and coherence of the Reform Agenda > 1.1.1 Consistency with the Objectives of the Western Balkans Facility

items.stated_text: Focusing on Digital Transition, the objectives are to establish secure digital infrastructures across the country, digitalise public administration and extend the available electronic public services offered to the citizens , thus simplifying administrative procedures for all services.
items.summary: The Reform Agenda's digital transition objectives are secure digital infrastructure, digitalised public administration and more electronic public services for citizens.

items.stated_text: The Reform Agenda submitted by North Macedonia aligns with the requirements outlined in Recital 19 and Articles 3.2 (k) and (l) of the Regulation, which underscore the importance of promoting digital transformation and digital skills as drivers for sustainable development and inclusive growth and emphasizes the necess ity to enhance innovation, research, and collaboration between academic institutions and industry to support digital transitions, thereby contributing to the facility's broader aim of promoting socio -economic convergence and minimizing discrepancies with t he EU.

items.stated_text: Through these proposed measures, North Macedonia demonstrates its commitment to undergo digital transformation and facilitate the achievement of the Union's digital targets , in line with Europe’s Digital Decade strategic framework .

items.stated_text: The proposed measures would enhance the country’s development of digital skills, digital transformation of businesses, secure and sustainable digital infrastructures, as well as further expand digitalisation of public services.
